t.name: Greenhorn Trail (upper)
t.description: Greenhorn is a mountain biking trail with man-made technical features integrated. Rollable jumps and dirt bermed turns.

t.name: Rise and Shine
t.description: Rise and Shine is used as access trail to top of Freeride area. Hike a bike section. Intended uphill push.

t.name: Rinse and Repeat
t.description: Rinse and Repeat is used as access to trail back to top of Freeride area. This is intended one-way (up) for bike push back to repeat the downhill trails from top.

t.name: Drip Torch Trail
t.description: This is most advanced mountain biking trail in the park. Difficult mountain biking trail with man-made technical features including wooden drops, a wooden wall ride, and mandatory air gap jumps. Full face helmet and knee/elbow pads highly recommended!

t.name: Little Brush Monkey
t.description: Short beginner skill loop just inside mountain biking area for training/classes.

t.name: Greenhorn Trail (lower)
t.description: Lower Greenhorn is more difficult than upper but has same character. Challenging mountain biking trail with man-made technical features. Rollable jumps (wooden tabled) with large dirt berm turns.

t.name: North Caddywhomper Way
t.description: North Caddywhomper is the main backbone/maintenance access path for XC north mountain biking area in L.L. Stub Stewart State Park. Beginner riders would have little difficulty on this wide dirt path.

t.name: Brush Monkey
t.description: Short skill loop inside mountain biking area for training.

t.name: Shoofly Trail
t.description: Shoofly is main cross-country mountain biking trail within L.L. Stub Stewart State Park. From North to South it follows eastern edge of Williams Creek drainage of Hares Canyon. Three large log stringer bridges cross several places on trail.

t.name: Crosstie Trail
t.description: Cross Tie begins near Hilltop Day Use parking area and connects to North mountain biking area trail system. It extends into mountain biking only area thru a skill filter/fence barrier to link with N. Caddywhomper. Hiking is permitted only to bike area.

t.name: Fernhill Wetlands Accessible Trail
t.description: Smooth, level paved pathway accessible to wheelchairs. walkers or other mobility aides.

t.name: Old Williams Creek Horseshoe
t.description: Original route of Williams Creek Horseshoe trail established 2007. Re-opened for equestrian users 2022.
